text:
Aisha Bello: Kicking off a tuning thread after yesterday’s first prod controlled failover (low-risk slice). We got good signal on the automation path, but a couple thresholds look off. Goal here: agree what we change in v0.2 + how we validate (monitor-only vs next test).

Aisha Bello: Observations (from dashboard + timeline):
- False positive-ish: `net_probe_loss` spiked in us-east for ~90s (some PoP-specific loss) and almost tripped degrade. Didn’t go to failover because quorum didn’t hit, but it did flip `region_health=DEGRADED` for 3 mins.
- False negative: tail latency went ugly (p99) before 5xx moved. Our `p99_latency_ms` threshold + window didn’t trigger until ~6 mins in.
- Hold-down worked (no flapping), but the “recover to HEALTHY” looks too fast; we bounced back after 4 mins even though error budget burn was still elevated.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also noting we paged on burn-rate before the state machine hit `DEGRADED` (which is backwards from what we want). If automation is going to be our first line, paging should align with “automation couldn’t fix” or “failed safe-to-failover checks”.

Miles Thornton: I pulled the state transitions + raw signals. For the `DEGRADED` flip, it was network probes from 2/6 vantage points (edge + synthetic) showing 8–12% loss. We’re currently using “any 2 probes in a region > 5% loss for 1m” as a contributing signal.

Peter Holtz: That’s too sensitive given probe noise. We knew this was a risk from the incident threads. We need to treat probe loss as “needs corroboration” unless it’s severe.

Sergio Costa: Here’s the relevant panel slice I’m looking at (failover dashboard v0.1). It’s basically:
- `net_probe_loss_percent{region}`
- `grpc_5xx_rate{region}`
- `request_p99_ms{region,route}`
When net loss pops, you also see streaming disconnects nudge up, but not enough to justify a region-level degrade.

Mina Haddad: From routing side: please keep in mind that any region-level `DEGRADED` is going to start enabling load shedding + fallback model variant selection for the scoped slice (even if we’re not failing over). So “soft” transitions still have customer impact.

Tomáš Novák: +1, and it also complicates on-call comms because folks see “degraded” and assume they need to do something, even if it’s just probe noise.

Aisha Bello: Proposal for network probes:
- Raise threshold from 5% -> 15% loss for “strong” signal
- Require duration >= 3m (instead of 1m)
- OR treat as weak signal: allow it to contribute to quorum only if either (a) p95 latency is elevated OR (b) 5xx is elevated.

Miles Thornton: I like weak-signal approach. Severe packet loss should still be able to trigger on its own though (e.g., >30% for 2m). Otherwise we’ll miss a partition.

Rafael Mendes: Can we model it as two bands?
- `NET_LOSS_WARN`: >15% for 3m (requires corroboration)
- `NET_LOSS_CRIT`: >30% for 2m (counts as strong, no corroboration)

Sergio Costa: That maps cleanly into the trigger engine config. It already supports weighted signals. We just haven’t turned weights on (currently boolean inputs -> quorum).

Aisha Bello: Yes. For v0.2 we can do weights without rewriting; Jordan said it’s a config + small code path (already in PR behind flag).

Peter Holtz: On the tail latency false negative: we should stop relying on p99 only. During the test, p99 spiked only for a subset of routes/models and got diluted at region aggregate.

Mina Haddad: Exactly. Region aggregate p99 is not representative when the problem is concentrated in a hot route/model. We should either evaluate at (region, route) and then roll up to region with max/percentile across routes.

Miles Thornton: The trigger engine can ingest route-scoped signals, but the health aggregator is currently publishing mostly region-level aggregates. We can publish `request_p95_ms{route}` and `p99{route}`.

Logan Wright: Telemetry side: we can publish route-scoped percentiles, but please limit cardinality. Do route groupings, not raw paths. Suggested: `route_class` (chat.completions, embeddings, rerank, etc) + `tier` (hosted/dedicated) + region. Not model id.

Aisha Bello: Fine. For the failover automation we care about customer impact (tier + route class) more than model granularity. Model fallback logic can live downstream.

Tomáš Novák: Also, can we incorporate queue depth / time-in-queue as earlier signal? Last incident + test: queuing got bad before 5xx.

Miles Thornton: We already have `scheduler_queue_depth` and `queue_latency_ms`. They’re in the “degradation controls” module but not in the region health quorum yet.

Rafael Mendes: I’m in favor of adding queue latency as a strong signal because it’s less noisy than p99 request latency and more directly tied to saturation. But we need to ensure it doesn’t trip during normal diurnal spikes.

Aisha Bello: We can do multi-window there. Something like:
- `queue_latency_p95_ms > 250` for 5m (warn)
- `queue_latency_p95_ms > 500` for 3m (crit)
Plus hysteresis.

Sergio Costa: Agree, and we can map that to burn-rate too. When queue latency is high, error budget burn tends to follow.

Mina Haddad: Please ensure we don’t trigger failover on pure saturation if other regions are also hot. That’s where “safe-to-failover” capacity checks should fail closed.

Miles Thornton: It did yesterday: safe-to-failover blocked the actual failover step because target region headroom dipped below 18% (we set min headroom 20%). That’s good.

Rafael Mendes: But we should make the operator experience better: if we’re blocked, the bot + dashboard should say *why* (headroom, dependency health, etc.) and recommend “shed load” vs “manual failover”. Right now it just says `SAFE_CHECK_FAILED`.

Sergio Costa: Noted. That’s more UX, but I can add a panel pulling reason codes from the audit log.

Aisha Bello: Back to recovery / flappiness: recovery threshold is currently symmetrical with trigger threshold and uses a 2m window. That’s too fast.

Miles Thornton: Yeah, we should do separate clear thresholds + longer clear windows. Something like:
- enter DEGRADED when condition holds for 3–5m
- clear DEGRADED only when *all* strong signals are below clear threshold for 10m
Also add a minimum dwell time in DEGRADED (e.g., 15m) unless we go to FAILED.

Peter Holtz: Minimum dwell time is helpful for operator comprehension. Otherwise dashboards look like noise.

Rafael Mendes: +1. But we also don’t want to pin in DEGRADED for 15m if we accidentally tripped due to a transient probe blip.

Aisha Bello: That’s where the probe tuning helps. If we lower sensitivity and require corroboration, we reduce accidental DEGRADED flips.

Logan Wright: Sharing a config sketch we can implement quickly (pseudocode). Please sanity check:
```yaml
signals:
  net_loss_warn:
    metric: net_probe_loss_percent
    threshold: 15
    window: 3m
    weight: 0.5
    requires_any:
      - grpc_5xx_rate_warn
      - request_latency_warn
  net_loss_crit:
    metric: net_probe_loss_percent
    threshold: 30
    window: 2m
    weight: 1.0

  request_latency_warn:
    metric: request_p95_ms
    group_by: [region, route_class, tier]
    threshold: 1800
    window: 4m
    weight: 0.75

  queue_latency_crit:
    metric: queue_latency_p95_ms
    threshold: 500
    window: 3m
    weight: 1.0

state_machine:
  degraded:
    enter_quorum: 1.5
    enter_window: 4m
    clear_quorum: 0.5
    clear_window: 10m
    min_dwell: 10m
```

Mina Haddad: For `request_p95_ms` threshold: 1800ms seems high for hosted chat. But it depends on route class. Can we do per-route thresholds?

Aisha Bello: Yes, per-route class thresholds are fine. Let’s start with:
- chat.completions: p95 > 2200ms (warn), p95 > 3500ms (crit)
- embeddings: p95 > 900ms (warn), p95 > 1500ms (crit)
We can adjust after we look at baselines. (Sergio, can you pull the last 30d p95/p99 distribution by route class?)

Sergio Costa: Yep. I’ll post screenshots + numbers in this thread once I have them.

Tomáš Novák: Operationally: we should write down the new “expected behavior” for on-call.
- DEGRADED is not necessarily failover; it can mean load-shed/fallback only.
- FAILED means progressive failover begins (if safe-to-failover passes).
And in monitor-only mode, make that explicit.

Rafael Mendes: +1, and for next iteration plan I want:
1) Land config changes behind `failover_trigger_v2` flag
2) Run in prod monitor-only for 7 days
3) During that week, label any near-triggers and validate whether it *should* have fired (false pos/neg review)
4) Then schedule next controlled failover (same low-risk scope) with Neha approval

Miles Thornton: Works. Also suggest a mini “replay” on last week’s incident metrics (offline) to see if new logic would have triggered earlier.

Aisha Bello: Good idea. We can do a shadow evaluation job reading TSDB and outputting what state would be at each minute.

Logan Wright: Careful on TSDB replay volume; keep it scoped to 2 regions + 3 route classes, 48h windows. Otherwise it’ll be expensive.

Mina Haddad: One more ask from routing: add a guardrail so we don’t go to FAILED if the impacted scope is only a single route class and we can mitigate via fallback within region. i.e., “prefer degrade + fallback” if that restores SLO.

Aisha Bello: That’s a product decision but aligns with “degraded but available”. For v0.2, we can add: require either multi-route impact OR error rate above crit. If it’s just one route class latency, we stay DEGRADED and lean on graceful degradation.

Rafael Mendes: I’m okay with that as long as we document it and don’t create blind spots. Let’s make it explicit: “failover is for region-level impairment; single-route issues are handled with load shedding/fallback unless 5xx crosses threshold.”

incident-bot: :information_source: Failover Orchestrator summary (prod test window)
- Scope: hosted / low-risk slice (5%)
- States observed: HEALTHY -> DEGRADED (3m) -> HEALTHY
- SAFE_CHECK failures: target_headroom_low (2 events)
- Audit log: https://console.redwood.example/internal/failover/audit?from=1714488000&to=1714499000

Sergio Costa: Baselines (last 30d, us-east/us-west, hosted):
- chat.completions p95: median 1100ms, p99: median 2400ms
- embeddings p95: median 420ms, p99: median 900ms
- rerank p95: median 280ms, p99: median 650ms
So Aisha’s warn thresholds seem fine. For chat, 2200ms p95 is roughly “bad day” territory.

Peter Holtz: Great. For the clear thresholds, can we do 80% of enter threshold? e.g., enter chat p95>2200, clear when <1700 for 10m.

Aisha Bello: Yes. Separate clear thresholds reduce oscillation.

Miles Thornton: Action items recap (please react / confirm):
1) Update trigger config:
   - net loss warn/crit split + corroboration requirements
   - route_class/tier-scoped latency signals (p95) + per-route thresholds
   - add queue latency as strong signal
   - longer clear window + clear thresholds + min dwell (10m)
2) Observability:
   - dashboard: show SAFE_CHECK failure reasons
   - add panel: “near trigger events” in monitor-only
3) Validation plan:
   - 7d monitor-only in prod (low-risk scope)
   - offline replay on last incident window
   - schedule next controlled failover after review

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: on all 3. I’ll open a Linear follow-up for the monitor-only week + review cadence.

Mina Haddad: :thumbsup: routing ok, with the note that route_class cardinality is controlled.

Tomáš Novák: :thumbsup: I’ll update runbook language once config lands (esp. DEGRADED semantics + when to page).

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: I’ll coordinate with Connor on flag rollout stages (monitor-only first), and we’ll align paging changes with the new states.

Sergio Costa: I’ll take dashboard updates + baseline docs. Expect PR by EOW.

Miles Thornton: I’ll implement the config + corroboration logic change (should be small). Will tag Aisha + Mina for review.

Rafael Mendes: Closing note: please keep a list of “known gaps” we’re explicitly accepting for v0.2 (e.g., model-specific issues, partial dependency failures). We’ll need that for Neha’s go/no-go on next test.

Aisha Bello: +1. I’ll add a section in the weekly notes doc and link it here once updated.
